title: XSS in user attributes
body: * Errbit version: master * OS: Ubuntu 18.04 #### Steps to reproduce: 1. Create a user with malicious name/username in your app 2. Cause an exception while logged in with that user 3. Errbit's `notices/_user_attributes` partial executes XSS #### Observed Results: * XSS through `.html_safe`-ing attributes (because of Rinku auto link) #### Expected Results: * No XSS :) #### Cause https://github.com/errbit/errbit/blob/e9ca15b842521d2ae536590c57c3db61fef19a3e/app/views/notices/_user_attributes.html.haml#L10 I'm not sure how to easily fix this but also keeping autolinking #### Example The thankfully friendly attacker delivered an example. The user caused the exception due to a missing length validation but every exception caused by a user might send untrusted data that shouldn't be blindly html_safe'd by errbit ``` "user" => { "name" => "\"> \"/> \"> \"/> /?regionConfirm=alert(document.cookie)});}}%3C/script%3E \"--> \">
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: Thanks for the report! Probably the solution here is to simply not autolink and not mark this as html_safe. I'm fine with losing the autolink email address feature if that's all it was.

comments.author: Participant 1

I'm not sure if users currently use intentional HTML in these places but what do you think about #1490?

Keeps autolinking which is frankly handy for something like the admin-hotlink but escapes the input beforehand.
